seed: first header after the pinned checkpoint
scope: Complete standalone transaction paths for a bounded direct-header counterbranch contest. Exact work under pinned regtest target, verified public fork challenge, provider branch response, outsider counterbranch, fixed payouts and timeout/equivocation paths. Direct verification of bounded challenger branches is still required; this does not solve long-chain optimistic challenge-input binding, candidate-set rebuttal or Groth16 admission. The no-more-proofs gate remains closed.

design.opening: An observer absent from setup supplies an actual validated conflicting branch with more work than the one-header original claim. The public committee presignature fixes the reply output; no challenger key is registered.
design.response: After the opening confirms, the provider signs its branch length once and supplies a validated extension using its registered original-hash key. The response creates a six-block public counterbranch/equivocation window before refund.
design.strongerCandidates: The opening candidate does not exhaust the contest. Any valid conflicting branch outweighing the signed response can pay the fixed client during the counterbranch window. No maximum-register oracle or further provider signature is needed in this bounded direct verifier.
design.inputBinding: The full short branches are verified directly in Script; publicly disclosed provider signatures bind original identity and response work to this graph. No claim is made that this solves general late-input binding for a compressed optimistic challenger proof.
design.exactWork: Every header must carry the pinned regtest target 0x207fffff. Its exact integer work is 2; both branches share a pinned checkpoint, so comparison of validated header counts is exactly comparison of cumulative work in this network.
design.setup: A local co-located MuSig2 setup drops its private committee object before funding. Provider WOTS secrets remain in RAM until the later claim/response selection; unused secrets are not exported. This is not a distributed key-deletion ceremony.

limits: At most three post-checkpoint headers; fixed regtest difficulty, first post-checkpoint header is the seed, and timestamps below the pinned pre-2038 upper bound.
Requires an honest observer able to confirm the relevant spend within the response/dispute windows; last-moment competing spends follow Bitcoin first-confirmation rules.
Megabyte scripts require nonstandard mining policy. Private Core mining is not evidence of public miner support.
Separate contract; no storage deal roots, long-chain Groth16 certificate admission, Binohash execution or integration with the funded storage v2 graph.

proofGate.reason: The bounded direct-header transaction milestone is verified. General long-chain optimistic challenge admission and full storage-bond integration must be concrete and tested before further proof jobs.
